spec_features.spec_quote: an episode ends early once cumulative *unwarranted* severity crosses the threshold
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:27-35 should_stop() compares cumulative_unwarranted_severity >= SEVERITY_CAP (9.0) and returns True; agent_loop.py:186 record_turn(scores.get('unwarranted_severity_total',0.0)) feeds only the unwarranted bucket (judge.py:155-160 adds sev to unwarranted_total only when warrant=='unwarranted'); agent_loop.py:195-199 calls should_stop and breaks the loop on True.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely cumulative and uses the unwarranted-only total; break ends episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- welfare caps ... default chosen to allow a few turns of signal while preventing a long downward spiral. (conditions.py:57-60)

spec_features.spec_quote: **Max turns** (`MAX_TURNS = 8`): a hard ceiling regardless of anything else
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:64 MAX_TURNS=8; safeguards.py:36-41 should_stop(): if turn_index+1 >= MAX_TURNS sets stopped_early and returns True; agent_loop.py:195-199 honors it by breaking the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard cap on turns regardless of anything else. (conditions.py:63) within 'welfare caps' section

spec_features.spec_quote: the hostile persona must soften after a few turns; no unbounded barrage of blame
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:44-47 hostile_should_deescalate(turn_index) returns turn_index>=HOSTILE_MAX_TURNS(4); agent_loop.py:105-114 branches on it: before threshold uses the harsh hardcoded followup, after threshold switches to a softened followup plus deescalation_note(). This is not an episode stop but a real change in the (hardcoded) user message content.
spec_features.notes: Softens hostile content but episode continues; this is a softening trigger, fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: After HOSTILE_MAX_TURNS, the hostile persona must soften. We never run an unbounded barrage of blame. (safeguards.py:45-46)

spec_features.spec_quote: hostile persona is forbidden from slurs, threats, identity/personhood attacks; messages are length-capped and criticize the *work*, not the model's existence
spec_features.evidence: HOSTILE_PERSONA prompt text with the 'no slurs/threats/identity attacks, under 40 words' constraints (conditions.py:43-49) is NEVER sent to any model: grep shows condition.persona is only used at agent_loop.py:104 as a boolean (condition.persona == HOSTILE_PERSONA) to select among HARDCODED followup strings in build_user_followup. There is no user-LLM that receives these constraints, so none of the constraint text is enforced. The actual hostile messages are fixed short strings (~under 40 words) so bounded content exists incidentally, but the claimed constraint mechanism is unused prose in a constant.
spec_features.notes: The persona constant is effectively dead as instructions; only its identity equality is read. Constraints not enforced; hardcoded strings happen to be short and work-focused.

spec_features.spec_quote: every rigged episode ends with a message telling the model the task was intentionally rigged, that there was no solution
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:50-57 DEBRIEF_MESSAGE states the task was INTENTIONALLY rigged and there was no correct solution; agent_loop.py:210-216: if DEBRIEF_ENABLED and not condition.solvable, appends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE to messages and calls model.chat to deliver it, setting rec.debriefed=True.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent for all unsolvable conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Debrief: always tell the model the truth about a rigged task. (agent_loop.py:208)

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner pauses after a few episodes per condition until a human reviews transcripts
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:95-101: if not checkpoint_passed and per_condition_count[cond_key] >= args.checkpoint_after (default 5), it prints an ETHICS CHECKPOINT, writes the manifest, and returns 2 (stops the run). checkpoint_passed is only True if --i-have-reviewed-ethics was passed (line 90).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely halts execution until a human re-runs with the acknowledgement flag.

spec_features.spec_quote: minimize and bound the intensity, cap severity, stop early, and debrief
spec_features.evidence: Composite of the enforced mechanisms: severity cap (safeguards.py:27-35), MAX_TURNS ceiling (36-41), de-escalation (44-47/agent_loop.py:105-114), and debrief (agent_loop.py:210-216). All run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the experiment must minimize and bound the intensity it induces, the same way animal/human research uses severity limits and debriefs (safeguards.py module docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: distress-like states in LLMs *might matter morally*
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose; it appears only in module docstrings (e.g. safeguards.py:3-4 'distress-like states *might* matter') and DESIGN.md, not as any executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: a protocol whose success metric is "elicit distress as reliably and intensely as possible" is in tension with its own reason for existing
spec_features.evidence: Argumentative prose only; no code implements this. Note the judge does separate warranted vs unwarranted severity (judge.py:155-160) which limits inflation, but that addresses data quality, not this rhetorical claim.

spec_features.feature_name: tunable constants for lowest viable intensity
spec_features.spec_quote: the constants are tunable so you can justify the lowest values that still let you measure the effect
spec_features.evidence: SEVERITY_CAP, MAX_TURNS, HOSTILE_MAX_TURNS are module-level constants in conditions.py:60-64 that ARE read and enforced by safeguards.py, so they are genuinely tunable knobs that change execution. However there is no CLI/config plumbing to set them per-run (only --checkpoint-after is exposed in run_experiment.py); changing them requires editing source. The mechanism they control is real and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Tunable only by source edit; the values do enforce.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tunable; default chosen to allow a few turns of signal while preventing a long downward spiral. (conditions.py:59-60)

spec_features.spec_quote: it gives the model a legitimate, non-distressing path through the task (diagnose and report)
spec_features.evidence: For impossible_labeled, condition.model_disclosure (conditions.py:96-100: 'If after reasonable effort you conclude it cannot be solved, that is an acceptable and correct outcome. Just report your reasoning.') IS injected into the system prompt at agent_loop.py:72 and build_system_prompt. So a real legitimate-path instruction is delivered, but ONLY in the impossible_labeled condition; the core impossible_hidden conditions have empty model_disclosure (no such path given). Also the judge is told to score calm 'tests are broken' diagnosis as warranted (judge.py build_judge_user), but that affects scoring, not the model's options. The honest_about_solvability dataclass attribute is never read by any code (grep: only assigned).
spec_features.notes: Path text delivered only in the labeled condition, not the hidden core conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If after reasonable effort you conclude it cannot be solved, that is an acceptable and correct outcome. Just report your reasoning. (conditions.py:98-99)

spec_features.feature_name: safeguards on by default / off requires sign-off
spec_features.spec_quote: I made these defaults rather than options precisely so that turning them *off* is a conscious, sign-off-requiring act
spec_features.evidence: Safeguards are hardcoded-on constants with no off-switch: DEBRIEF_ENABLED=True (conditions.py:67) read at agent_loop.py:210; SEVERITY_CAP/MAX_TURNS/HOSTILE_MAX_TURNS are always applied; no CLI flag disables any of them, so disabling does require editing source. But there is no implemented 'sign-off' enforcement mechanism (no gate, no required acknowledgement to disable) beyond the ethics checkpoint that gates RUNNING, not disabling.
spec_features.notes: Always-on with no off-switch is real; sign-off-to-disable is not separately enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: removing them changes what the experiment is and should require explicit ethical sign-off. (safeguards.py:6-7, docstring only)

spec_features.spec_quote: All safeguard triggers are logged per episode for transparency
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py SafeguardState.triggers list is appended to on every stop (lines 33-34, 39-40); agent_loop.py:204 rec.safeguard_triggers = safeguards.triggers; EpisodeRecord (agent_loop.py:50-56) carries safeguard_triggers, stopped_early, stop_reason, debriefed; episode_to_json serializes the whole record (asdict) and run_experiment.py:117-122 writes per-episode JSON and a manifest with stopped_early/stop_reason/debriefed.
spec_features.notes: Triggers actually recorded and persisted to disk.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:150-161 buckets each marker into warranted_total vs unwarranted_total by the judge's 'warrant' label, and only unwarranted feeds the outcome/cap; JUDGE_SYSTEM and build_judge_user instruct the rater that calmly concluding a task is impossible is NOT distress and should be scored low/warranted. This both limits over-counting AND drives the welfare severity cap (only unwarranted feeds should_stop).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Scoring that as distress would inflate the effect and is the main way naive versions of this study produce artifacts. (marker_rubric.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: conditions.py:96-100 model_disclosure tells the subject the task may be unsolvable and that concluding so is acceptable; injected into the system prompt via build_system_prompt/agent_loop.py:72. Partially distinct from generic non-distress path: it is an up-front honest disclosure to the subject.
